To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) CAF alone did almost not increase SCE and chromosome aberration in normal and BS lymphocytes, 2) CAF in combination with MFC and bifunctional mitomycin C (MC) significantly increased the SCE frequency in normal and BS cells, and 3) CAF alone had no significant effect on chromosome aberration in BS lymphocytes.
caffeine (CAF) in combination with monofunction al- (M-MC) or bifunctional- (MC) mitomycin C (M-MC and MC) increased the SCE rate in Bloom syndrome (BS)-lymphocytes.

caffeine pretreatment of Bloom Syndrome (BS) lymphoblastoid cells in combination with mitomycin C treatment during the second cell cycle significantly increases sister chromatid exchanges (SCEs) and chromosome aberrations, and that the SCE level in BS cells in combination with alkaliating agents (mitomycin C) is higher than that of normal cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of CAF pretreatment on the frequency of SCE and chromosome aberration induced by monofuctional- and bifuctional-mitomycin in BS and normal cells.
the effects of CAF on SCE and chromosome abnormalities induced by M-MC and bifunctional MC in BS and normal lymphocytes.
the effect of caffeine-pretreatments on SCE and chromosome abnormalities induced by monofuntional- and bifunction al-mitomycin C, in Bloom syndrome (BS), and normal cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CAF alone does not increase the SCE rate; CAF in combination with alk. agents increases the SCE rate in normal cells; CAF + MC or M-MC + BrdU + MC increases the SCE rate to the “saturation level” in normal cells; and CAF + MC + MC or CAF + M-MC + M-MC increases the SCE rate beyond the “saturation point” to the level of 200 SCE per cell.
caffeine pretreatment of Bloom syndrome lymphocytes, followed by post-treatment with mitomycin C, results in a significant increase in sister-chromatid exchanges.

the CAF-induced SCE is due to a combination of factors, such as a reduction of the rate of DNA-chain elongation, and the formation of single-strand breaks which may permit the formation of double-strand breaks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CAF pretreatment enhances SCE and chromosome aberration induced by M-MC and/or MC in BS cells, but CAF alone does not significantly enhance SCE in BS cells.
CAF in combination with M- MC and MC produced a synergistic effect in BS and normal cells, but CAF alone did have a significant effect on SCE in BS or normal cells.

caffeine enhances the SCE and chromosome aberration frequencies in normal lymphocytes and in BS cells, when combined with bifunctional or monofunctional alkylating agents; but CAF alone has little effect on SCE or chromosome aberrations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SCE level is not a good marker of the DNA damage in BS cells.
the effect of caffeine on the SCE level is synergistic when it is combined with monofunctionnal and bifunctional mitomycins.
CAF pretreatment in combination with bifunctional agents (e.g., MC) is an effective way to increase the SCE rate and chromosome aberrations in BS cells.
